arxiv-2106-05451.creator: Jintae Kim, Jung Hoon Han
arxiv-2106-05451.description: Abstract We propose a lattice spin model on a cubic lattice that shares many of the properties of the 3D toric code and the X-cube fracton model. The model, made of ℤ 3 \mathbb{Z}_{3} degrees of freedom at the links, has the vertex, the cube, and the plaquette terms. Being a stabilizer code the ground states are exactly solved.

arxiv-2209-08333.description: Abstract Edge Computing is a promising technology to provide new capabilities in technological fields that require instantaneous data processing. Researchers in areas such as machine and deep learning use extensively edge and cloud computing for their applications, mainly due to the significant computational and storage resources that they provide.

arxiv-2502-14079.title: Population Dynamics Control with Partial Observations
arxiv-2502-14079.creator: Zhou Lu, Y.Jennifer Sun, Zhiyu Zhang
arxiv-2502-14079.description: Abstract We study the problem of controlling population dynamics—a class of linear dynamical systems evolving on the probability simplex—from the perspective of online non-stochastic control. While Golowich et al. (2024) analyzed the fully observable setting, we focus on the more realistic, partially observable case, where only a low-dimensional representation of the state is accessible.

arxiv-2503-21489.title: Shape modeling of longitudinal medical images: from diffeomorphic metric mapping to deep learning
arxiv-2503-21489.creator: Edwin Tay, Nazli Tümer, Amir A. Zadpoor
arxiv-2503-21489.description: Abstract Living biological tissue is a complex system, constantly growing and changing in response to external and internal stimuli. These processes lead to remarkable and intricate changes in shape. Modeling and understanding both natural and pathological (or abnormal) changes in the shape of anatomical structures is highly relevant, with applications in diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic healthcare.

pmc-10649744.creator: Alexandra Höpfinger, Andreas Schmid, Leonie Schweitzer, Marissa Patz, Anja Weber, Andreas Schäffler, Thomas Karrasch
pmc-10649744.description: Understanding the complex interactions between metabolism and the immune system (“metaflammation”) is crucial for the identification of key immunomodulatory factors as potential therapeutic targets in obesity and in cardiovascular diseases. Cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide (CAMP) is an important factor of innate immunity and is expressed in adipocytes. CAMP, therefore, might play a role as an adipokine in metaflammation and adipose inflammation.

pmc-11428269.description: Pulmonary artery hypertension (PAH) is characterised by increased pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) resulting in elevated pressure in the pulmonary artery supplying the pulmonary circulation. Disease of the right ventricle (RV) often manifests as a result of PAH placing excessive pressure on the right side of the heart.

pmc-11490723.title: Carnitine is a friend in HFpEF and foe in HFrEF
pmc-11490723.creator: Huiqing Wang, Haoran Wei, Mingming Zhao, Junfang Wu, Min Fei, Nan Lin, Rui Zhan, Qingyuan Liu, Qi Zhang, Xiaodong Yao, Yufei Wu, Wenxin Shan, Hongtu Cui, Liang Ji, Bing Pan, Lu Fang, Yujie Zhu, Xin Li, Yansong Guo, Dao Wen Wang, Lemin Zheng
pmc-11490723.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryHeart failure (HF) is a global concern, particularly HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), lacking effective treatments. Understanding the differences of metabolic profiles between HFpEF and HFrEF (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) patients is crucial for therapeutic advancements. In this study, pseudotargeted metabolomics was employed to analyze for disparities of plasma metabolic profiles between HFpEF and HFrEF in two cohorts: discovery (n = 514) and validation (n = 3368). Plasma-free carnitine levels were significant changed in HF patients.

pmc-11504776.description: Background:Cervical cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality among women in India. Screening can help in early detection and improve outcomes. However, uptake remains low, especially in rural areas. Understanding multidimensional factors influencing screening in local contexts is essential to promote equitable access.

pmc-12592145.title: Functional impacts of lactylation in Hypoxia‒primed mesenchymal stromal cells
pmc-12592145.creator: Fanyi Zhao, Qixing Tang, Jie Liu
pmc-12592145.description: Hypoxic culture (1–5% O2) significantly enhances the biological activity and therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) by activating the HIF-1α signaling pathway. This activation promotes stemness maintenance, enhances proliferative capacity, and improves immunomodulatory functions, such as upregulating the secretion of indoleamine 2,3‒dioxygenase (IDO) and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2).

pmc-12689005.title: Extensive multifocal extranodal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving parotid, breast, gastrointestinal tract, and dorsal spine: a case report
pmc-12689005.creator: Syed Hameed-Ul-Hassan Shah, Syed Ibraheem Ul Hassan Ramzi, Hooria Ahmad Qureshi, Jeevan Gyawali, Waseem Sattar
pmc-12689005.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction:Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with extranodal involvement in up to 40% of cases. However, simultaneous involvement of multiple extranodal sites without dominant nodal disease remains very rare and diagnostically challenging.Case presentation:We report a case of a 61-year-old female with a history of hypertension and recurrent anemia, who presented with progressive swelling in the left breast and parotid area, and systemic symptoms.

pmc-12842460.title: Assessment of Radiographic Image Texture in the Maxilla and Mandible Around Titanium Inserts Used for Osteosynthesis of Dentofacial Deformities

pmc-12842460.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: In the treatment of dentofacial deformities, miniplates and screws made of titanium and its alloys (Ti6Al4V) are currently used for osteosynthesis of bone segments, which is due to the high biocompatibility of these materials. Despite the unquestionable advantages of titanium implants, there is an ongoing discussion about their potential negative impact on the human body, both at the implantation site and systemically.

pmc-13614918.creator: Styliana Georgiou, Triantafyllos Stylianopoulos, Chrysovalantis Voutouri
pmc-13614918.description: Precise prediction of cancer therapy response remains challenging because conventional biomarkers capture molecular features but overlook the physical state of tumors.
